register.description: Controls various parameters of the cotroller state.

bitfield.description: 0 OSPI 32bit mode enabled. 1 OSPI 32bit mode disabled Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
0 XIP Prefetch Enabled. 1 XIP prefetch disabled Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
0 OSPI DDR mode enabled. 1 OSPI DDR mode disabled Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
0 Block address within ECC calculation, 1 Block address not within ECC calculation Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
1 select security, 0 disable security Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
0 ECC disabled. 1 ECC enabled Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: This FRAG_ADR is the address of a request that frag_hi or frag_lo boundary occurs

bitfield.description: This address is used to determine the boundary of frag_hi and flag_lo Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: The FRAG_CTL determins which frag region is fragmented

bitfield.description: When set any address greater than or equal to frag_addr will be fragmented to 16 bits Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
When set any address less than frag_addr will be fragmented to 16 bits Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: The End of Interrupt (EOI) MISC Register allows the CPU to acknowledge completion of an interrupt by writing to the EOI for MISC interrupt sources. An eoi_write signal will be generated and another interrupt will be triggered if interrupt sources remain. This register will be reset one cycle after it has been written to.

bitfield.description: Write with bit position of targeted interrupt. (E.g. Ext FSS ECC is bit 0). Upon write, level interrupt will clear and if un-serviced will issue another pulse interrupt Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: The IRQ_STATUS_RAW register allows the interrupt sources to be manually set when writing a 1 to a specific bit. Write 0: No action Write 1: Set event Read 0: No event pending Read 1: Event pending

bitfield.description: Write is not aligned to 32B boundary or not a multiple of 32B Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
ECC error on 2 bits. Not correctable Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
ECC error on 1 bits. correctable Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: The IRQ_STATUS register allows the interrupt sources to be manually cleared when writing a 1 to a specific bit. Write 0: No action Write 1: Clear event Read 0: No event pending Read 1: Event pending

bitfield.description: Write is not aligned to 32B boundary or not a multiple of 32B Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
ECC error on 2 bits. Not correctable Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
ECC error on 1 bits. correctable Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: The IRQ_ENABLE_SET register allows the interrupt sources to be manually enabled when writing a 1 to a specific bit. Write 0: No action Write 1: Enable event Read 0: Event is disabled Read 1: Event is enabled

bitfield.description: Write is not aligned to 32B boundary or not a multiple of 32B Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
ECC error on 2 bits. Not correctable Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
ECC error on 1 bits. correctable Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: The IRQ_ENABLE_CLR register allows the interrupt sources to be manually disabled when writing a 1 to a specific bit. Write 0: No action Write 1: Disable event Read 0: Event is disabled Read 1: Event is enabled

bitfield.description: Write is not aligned to 32B boundary or not a multiple of 32B Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
ECC error on 2 bits. Not correctable Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
ECC error on 1 bits. correctable Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: This defines the start of the ECC region in 4KBytes steps.

bitfield.description: This defines the start of the ECC region in 4KBytes steps. Address start = {start[19:0], 0x000}0x0 means the start is 0x0000_0000 0x1 means the start is 0x0000_10000xA means the start is 0x0000_A000Note the offset + size should be <= 4GBytes, wrap around is not supported. Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: This defines the size of the ECC region in 4KBytes steps.

bitfield.description: This defines the size of the ECC region in 4KBytes steps0x0 means the size is zero and disabled 0x1 means the size is 4KBytes0xA means the size is 40KBytes0xF_FFFF means the size is 4GBytesNote the offset + size should be <= 4GBytes, wrap around is not supported. Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: The ERR_ECC_BLOCK_ADR register holds the current top of stack ECC error block address, this is only valid when the ecc_err_valid is set

bitfield.description: ECC 32 byte aligned block address Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: The ERR_ECC_TYPE register holds the current top of stack ECC error info, this is only valid when the ecc_err_valid is set

bitfield.description: When set indicates that there is valid ECC error information available, Writing a one to this register will pop the top of the stack Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
When set indicates that there was a single error detected within the address field Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
When set indicates that there was a single error detected within the MAC field Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
When set indicates that there was a single error detected within the High Data word Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
When set indicates that there was a single error detected within the Low Data word Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
When set indicates that there was a double error detected for the block Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
hen set indicates that there was a single error detected for the block Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n

register.description: The ERR_WRT_TYPE register holds the current top of stack write error info. this is only valid when the wrt_err_valid is set

bitfield.description: When set indicates that there is valid write error information available, Writing a one to this register will pop the top of the stack Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
When set indicates that there was a write error due to a non-contiguous byte enables Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
When set indicates that there was a write error due to a non-aligned address Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
Indicates the Route ID for the Initiator that caused the write error Reset Source: vbus_mod_g_rst_n
